review_notes: I read all 112 lines of the target. I also read the two lemmas the decrement proofs call, `dyadic_heat_increment_lower_mass` (UniformHeatMassIncrement.lean) and `gaussian_dyadic_heat_increment_envelope` (ActualHeatEnvelope.lean). Then I searched the project for uses of `dyadic_radius_square_succ`, `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` and `dyadicHeatGram_coe`. Both lower-level lemmas state their conclusion as a difference of `cutoffHeatGram` values at times s^2 and s^2/4. So each dyadic decrement proof has to repeat one step: unfold both `dyadicHeatGram` terms, then turn the (i+1)-st time (R/2^(i+1))^2 into (R/2^i)^2/4. The same 5–6 line block appears in `dyadicHeatGram_lower`, in `dyadicHeatGram_upper`, and in `dyadicHeatGram_upper_supported` (SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean, lines 77–81). A pole-generic copy also appears twice in DyadicHeatAt.lean, using `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr_at`. I found nothing else in the file that meets the rubric. `dyadic_radius_square_succ`, `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr`, `dyadicHeatGram_coe` and `dyadicHeatGram_isPositive` are short, routine helpers, each used once or wrapping existing API. One caveat: the proposed lemma has not been compiled. Its statement contains proof terms (`sq_pos_of_pos hs`, `div_pos … (by norm_num)`), and it relies on proof irrelevance to match the call sites. That is the same mechanism the existing `rw [hnext]` already relies on, but it is still untested.

findings.problem: Both decrement theorems (and `dyadicHeatGram_upper_supported` in SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean) repeat the same argument that identifies the dyadic Gram decrement with the heat Gram increment over [s^2/4, s^2], where s = R/2^i. Each copy rebuilds the positivity proof of (R/2^(i+1))^2 and the positivity of s^2/4, calls `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` with `dyadic_radius_square_succ R i`, then runs `simp only [sub_apply, inner_sub_right, dyadicHeatGram_coe]` and `rw [hnext]`. Lines 72–77 and 101–105 are verbatim copies; SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean lines 77–81 is a third copy. This step is the one mathematical fact that links the dyadic family to the lemmas `dyadic_heat_increment_lower_mass` and `gaussian_dyadic_heat_increment_envelope`, whose conclusions use exactly the times s^2 and s^2/4. Yet the fact is never stated on its own.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the following just after `dyadicHeatGram_isPositive`, before `variable {U}`, so that `U` is still explicit:

theorem dyadicHeatGram_sub_inner {R lambda : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (i : ℕ)
    (v : Euclidean n) :
    ⟪v, ((dyadicHeatGram μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda i : Euclidean n →L[ℝ] Euclidean n) -
      (dyadicHeatGram μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda (i + 1) : Euclidean n →L[ℝ] Euclidean n)) v⟫_ℝ =
    ⟪v, cutoffHeatGram μ hQ hk χ.weight.continuous (χ.hasCompactSupport μ hQ) U
        (sq_pos_of_pos (div_pos hR (show 0 < (2 : ℝ) ^ i by positivity))) p lambda v⟫_ℝ -
      ⟪v, cutoffHeatGram μ hQ hk χ.weight.continuous (χ.hasCompactSupport μ hQ) U
        (div_pos (sq_pos_of_pos (div_pos hR (show 0 < (2 : ℝ) ^ i by positivity)))
          (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 4)) p lambda v⟫_ℝ := by
  have hs : 0 < R / (2 : ℝ) ^ i := div_pos hR (by positivity)
  simp only [sub_apply, inner_sub_right, dyadicHeatGram_coe]
  rw [cutoffHeatGram_time_congr μ hQ hk U χ (lambda := lambda)
    (sq_pos_of_pos (show 0 < R / (2 : ℝ) ^ (i + 1) from div_pos hR (by positivity)))
    (div_pos (sq_pos_of_pos hs) (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) < 4)) (dyadic_radius_square_succ R i)]

The body is just the block that is currently duplicated.

findings.benefit: Each decrement proof then reads as: apply the heat-increment lemma, then identify the dyadic decrement with that increment. The fragile time-reindexing step, with its hand-built positivity proofs and the s^2/4 = (R/2^(i+1))^2 rewrite, lives in one named lemma. That removes three verbatim copies. If `dyadicHeatGram`'s time parameterization or the form of the increment lemmas changes, only the helper needs updating, not every decrement proof. The lemma is also a reusable interface for any later dyadic bound.
